title: Make athena drain work cli-channel (ask --later) queued requests
summary: queued_work in steward.rs keeps only channel "steward", so requests from `ask --later` (channel "cli") are never drained. Change it to a channel-set filter (steward and cli), keep ordering and retry unchanged, fix the stale docs, and prove it with tests using fresh ids. Audience: the user who queues requests and expects drain to work them.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for both channels; cargo test and clippy pass.
Fix the shared selection function, not a per-id case.
Tests run drain with a cli-channel request.
Docs and decision entry written for an outside reader.
One focused filter change plus its docs and tests.
Verifier runs the test, clippy and fmt commands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: `ask --later` records channel "cli"; the producer must confirm this in the code before filtering.
Gate commands (test, clippy, fmt) are a standing definition of done, listed as one criterion each at the end.
Earlier failures were unmet criteria: no job ids in non-test code, docs corrected in all places, gate results reported. The producer should map each criterion to evidence before reporting.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in steward.rs, using fresh job ids, shows queued_work returns unread Queued requests from both the steward and cli channels, oldest first (ties by job id), and excludes non-Queued jobs and other channels. Run `cargo test -p athena-core queued_work`.
A drain test with a cli-channel queued request (fresh id) shows drain lists and works it like a steward item. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
Existing drain ordering and retry/thrash tests pass unedited. Run `cargo test`.

The change in queued_work is a channel-set filter with no job-id special case. `git diff` shows none of the ids 20261015-215658-6ejp, 20261015-215701-cqn8, 20261015-215703-px13, 20261015-225907-kb92 in non-test code.

No doc comment still says drain takes only the steward channel: REQUEST_CHANNEL and queued_work in steward.rs, drain.rs, and docs/decisions.md. Grep for the old wording finds none outside historical entries.
A new docs/decisions.md entry and a CHANGELOG.md line record the change and why.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, and `cargo test` passes in full.

out_of_scope: Changing drain ordering, retry, or thrash rules
Draining channels other than steward and cli
Building the completion gate proposed by the introspection
departures: Slightly lower pass chance: this is a retry of a repeatedly failed job with many cross-file criteria.
